question: to the Commission Estrella Galán (The Left), Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), Vicent Marzà Ibáñez (Verts/ALE), Leire Pajín (S&D), Rima Hassan (The Left), Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Carolina Morace (The Left), Vladimir Prebilič (Verts/ALE), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Pernando Barrena Arza (The Left), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Rosa Serrano Sierra (S&D), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Damien Carême (The Left), Arash Saeidi (The Left), Giorgos Georgiou (The Left), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Michael McNamara (Renew) Subject:

On 30 March 2026, the Israeli Parliament adopted a law stipulating that Palestinians convicted by Israeli military courts of what those authorities define as ‘deadly attacks’ would be executed by hanging within 90 days. The implementation of this law is clearly discriminatory, cruel and against human rights. The law has also faced internal opposition in Israel, as well as from the Council of Europe, which considers that its adoption ‘represents a serious regression’. 1.

What is the Commission’s view of statements made by countries such as Australia, Britain, France, Spain, Germany and Italy that consider this measure to call into question Israel’s commitments to democratic principles?

The measure once again violates Article 2 of the EU-Israel Trade Agreement, which states that relations between the two sides are based on respect for human rights and democratic principles. Does the Commission intend to take appropriate measures to immediately suspend the EU trade agreement with Israel?
Does the Commission intend to take any initiative to ensure the legal protection of incarcerated Palestinians who could be victims of this measure?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: César Luena (S&D).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2026) The EU has a principled position against the death penalty in all cases and in all circumstances. The approval of the Death Penalty Law by the Israeli Parliament marks a grave regression from Israel’s long upheld moratorium and from its own commitments. The EU is deeply concerned about the de facto discriminatory character of the Law1. Consistent with the EU global efforts towards universal abolition of the death penalty, the EU urges Israel to abide by its previous principled position and with its obligations under international law, as well as its commitment to democratic principles, as reflected also in the provisions of the EU-Israel Association Agreement2. The death penalty is a violation of the right to life and cannot be executed without violation of the absolute right to be free from torture and other ill-treatment. In 2024, a review of the EU-Israel Association agreement concluded that Israel would be in breach of Article 2 (human rights clause) of the said Association Agreement. Following the review, and in light of the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza, the Commission’s President announced a set of measures, including the suspension of certain trade-related provisions of the EU-Israel Association Agreement. This requires the support of the qualified majority of Member States. Discussions are ongoing in the Council. Measures ensuring the legal protection of persons incarcerated in third countries fall under the jurisdiction of the third countries in question. Nevertheless, the EU will use the tools at its disposal and urge Israel not to enforce the Death Penalty Law, which is currently under review by the Supreme Court.
